# Candakumāracariya (Cp 7)

**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1

**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Conduct of Prince Canda

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Candakumāracariya* ("The Conduct of Prince Canda") is the seventh poem in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* (CP 1.7), situated within its opening section focusing on the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramī*) [Appleton, Buddha as Storyteller; Bareau, Les récits canoniques du Cariyāpiṭaka; SuttaCentral]. Composed of six verses, the text narrates a past life in which the Bodhisatta was born as Prince Canda, the son of a sovereign in the city of Pupphavatī, who renounced sacrificial rites [Appleton, Buddha as Storyteller; Bareau, Les récits canoniques du Cariyāpiṭaka]. The narrative represents a condensed version of the *Khaṇḍahāla-jātaka* (JA 542), which recounts how a king—deceived by an evil brahmin—planned a great sacrifice of his family, including Prince Canda, who was eventually saved through his wife's declaration of truth and the intervention of the god Sakka [Appleton, Buddha as Storyteller]. Naomi Appleton observes that the *Cariyāpiṭaka* condenses and omits substantial narrative elements from the Jātaka to focus specifically on the perfections required for buddhahood [Appleton, Buddha as Storyteller].

SuttaCentral records no curated parallels for the text, though it lists a modern English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identified no internal Pali text reuse, but automatically aligned portions of the text (§3.2–3.4) with the Tibetan translation of the *Ārya-ṛṣi-vyāparipṛcchā-nāma-mahāyānasūtra* (D0093, §284a-7) [DharmaNexus].
